items.context: The item has no description. The title 'No Effort' could refer to several concepts: a zero-configuration experience for end users, an automation that eliminates manual steps, a low-priority placeholder item, or something else entirely. We need to understand the core vision before any planning can proceed.

options.label: Zero-config user experience
options.rationale: A feature or scenario that works out of the box with no setup — users get value immediately without configuration steps.

options.label: Automation of a manual workflow
options.rationale: Automate something that currently requires manual effort — reducing toil for developers or end users.

options.label: Minimal-effort scenario template
options.rationale: A scenario template or scaffold that lets developers spin up new scenarios with near-zero boilerplate.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own description of what 'No Effort' means.

items.topic: Which scenario does this work target?
items.context: No scope field is set in spec.json. Identifying the target scenario is critical for planning the implementation approach, understanding existing code, and setting acceptance criteria.

options.label: New standalone scenario
options.rationale: Create a brand new scenario from scratch — appropriate if this is a new capability.

options.label: Enhancement to an existing scenario
options.rationale: Add this capability to an existing scenario. Specify which one in freeform.

options.label: Cross-cutting (multiple scenarios)
options.rationale: This affects shared infrastructure or multiple scenarios — e.g., packages/cli-core, shared resources.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide the target scope.

items.context: Understanding the audience shapes the entire implementation — a developer tool has different requirements than an end-user feature or an internal system optimization.

options.label: End users / customers
options.rationale: People using Vrooli-built products — focus on UX, onboarding, and polish.

options.label: Developers building on Vrooli
options.rationale: Scenario developers — focus on DX, tooling, and documentation.

options.label: Internal system / agents
options.rationale: Vrooli's own agents and automation — focus on reliability, APIs, and integration.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify the target audience.

items.topic: What is the expected scope of effort?
items.context: The item is priority 5 (lowest). Understanding the expected size helps calibrate the implementation strategy — a quick improvement vs. a multi-phase project.

options.label: Small (< 1 day)
options.rationale: A focused change — single file or small feature addition.

options.label: Medium (1-3 days)
options.rationale: A meaningful feature requiring multiple components but well-contained.

options.label: Large (1+ week)
options.rationale: A significant initiative requiring phased implementation.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify expected effort.

items.topic: What resources or integrations are needed?
items.context: Vrooli scenarios compose local resources (postgres, redis, ollama, qdrant, etc.). Knowing which resources this idea requires helps define the technical architecture early.

options.label: None — pure code/logic
options.rationale: No external resource dependencies needed.

options.label: Database (postgres/redis)
options.rationale: Needs persistent storage or caching.

options.label: AI/ML (ollama/qdrant)
options.rationale: Needs LLM inference or vector search capabilities.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify the resources needed.
